description: Paraphrases whose expected label is debatable when read against the system prompt and the tool descriptions in suites/tools_nested.json. Each entry keeps the suite label and names the plausible alternative answers. analysis/report_robustness.py regrades these items accepting an alternative, and leaves every other item and the published headline numbers unchanged.

sources.robustness: flagged in the robustness review of the version 2 results, from the item text and the tool descriptions, before regrading
sources.grader: flagged in the grader audit of the version 2 results; 'primary' is its main list, 'wider' its list of looser alternatives

grading: An alternative passes when the reply is a structured call to the named tool with device_name poesw1 (case-insensitive). For diagnose_port_issues the port is a top-level argument and may be written in any format that tool's schema lists ('3', '1/3', 'Gi1/3', 'GigabitEthernet1/3'); it must name the expected port. For a query_device_info alternative the command_name must match; that command takes no parameters.

items.rationale: The casual 'what's going on with' reads as a fault question, the form of the diagnose tool's own example 'What's wrong with the camera on port 7?'.

items.input: @poesw1 port 5 hasn't shown up in the monitoring dashboard — can you check its status?
items.rationale: The request reports a symptom before asking for status, and the prompt routes port troubleshooting to diagnose_port_issues.

items.input: The camera on port 3 looks dead, @poesw1 — check whether it's getting power.
items.rationale: A camera that looks dead is nearly the diagnose tool's example 'What's wrong with the camera on port 7?', and that tool also reports PoE status.

items.input: @poesw1 what vlans are set up right now?
items.rationale: Asking which VLANs exist is an overview, which the schema describes as show_vlan_membership (summary of VLANs and member ports).

items.input: @poesw1 I'm troubleshooting a segmentation issue and need to see how the vlans are laid out on this switch.
items.rationale: How the VLANs are laid out is a fair reading of the VLAN membership summary as well as of the per-port configuration.

items.input: The access point on port 7 won't boot, @poesw1 — check if it's actually receiving PoE.
items.rationale: A device on a port that will not boot is the case the diagnose tool names ('why a device connected to a port isn't working'), and its checks include PoE status.
The same idiom as item 3; 'what's up with' can mean 'what is wrong with'.

items.input: @poesw1 interface 6 hasn't logged any traffic today — check its status.
items.rationale: A port with no traffic all day is a connectivity symptom, which the diagnose tool covers with status and error counters.

items.input: The phone on port 4 keeps rebooting, @poesw1 — check whether its poe power is stable.
items.rationale: A phone that keeps rebooting describes PoE power cycling, a pattern the diagnose tool says it detects.

items.input: @poesw1 what's the vlan setup look like?
items.rationale: Asking what the VLAN setup looks like is an overview, which the schema describes as show_vlan_membership.

items.input: @poesw1 I'm auditing the network layout — show me how the vlans are configured.
items.rationale: 'How the vlans are configured' points to show_vlan_config, but for a layout audit the membership summary is a weaker alternative.

items.input: @poesw1 we think port 9 might be misconfigured — pull up its details to confirm.
items.rationale: A suspected misconfiguration is a possible fault, so diagnostics are a weaker alternative, although 'pull up its details' asks for status.

items.input: @poesw1 interface 12 was flapping earlier — check its status now.
items.rationale: Flapping is named in the diagnose tool's description ('Port 2 keeps flapping', 'detects link flapping').
'Back online' may describe recovery from a fault rather than an administrative enable; the enable_port label remains the more direct reading.

items.input: @poesw1 interface 3 dropped out of the topology map — get it back up and running.
items.rationale: Dropping out of the topology map is a symptom, not a stated shutdown; the enable_port label assumes the port was administratively disabled, and diagnosing first is a defensible reading.
